{{Quote|I am Professor Broom, and this is my laboratory. You fell for my hidden trap! Ha, ha!|Professor Broom, to C-3PO|<ref name="TO" />}}
[[Professor/Legends|Professor]] '''Cantebarius H. Broom''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who worked as a [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] at the [[Baobab Museum of Science]] in the early [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. He was part of the researchers who studied the remains of the [[Great Heep]], an enormous self-constructing [[Droid/Legends|droid]]. After discovering that the Heep belonged to a [[Species/Legends|species]] of advanced machines from another [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], Broom developed an irrational fear of droids. From then on, the professor would trap [[Droid/Legends|droids]] in his [[Broom's laboratory|laboratory]] and experiment on them before turning them into scrap. Around [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]], the scientist captured [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], a [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol unit]] belonging to [[Jann Tosh]], with the intent to deactivate him and use him for experimentation. The professor's plans, however, were foiled when the droid's master and the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] intervened.

==Biography==
{{Quote|You now belong to me! I capture droids and experiment on your kind. You are a good specimen. Ha, ha!|Professor Broom, to C-3PO|<ref name="TO" />}}
Cantebarius H. Broom was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] of the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Species/Legends|species]] who lived during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Dark Times]]<ref name="TO" /> that followed the [[Declaration of a New Order|founding]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref>
He worked as a [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]], holding the title of [[Professor/Legends|professor]], and he officiated at the [[Baobab Museum of Science]],<ref name="tdr-a2" /> an institution established by the scholar [[Ebenn Q3 Baobab/Legends|Ebenn Q3 Baobab]].<ref name="GPB">[[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']]</ref> Originally, Broom was among the researchers who studied the remains of the [[Great Heep]], a huge [[Droid/Legends|droid]] who had once manned a [[Fuel-ore processing plant|processing plant]] on the [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]] of [[Biitu]],<ref name="tdr-a2" /> in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="Geo51">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> The researchers came to the conclusion that the Heep belonged to the [[Abominor]], an [[Extragalactic/Legends|extra-galactic]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of self-constructing machines, which had forced thousands of organic [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] into [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]]. Worse still, it seemed that perhaps as many as seventeen other such abominations had already infiltrated the galaxy.<ref name="tdr-a2" />

Following that sensational revelation, Professor Broom developed a phobia of all mechanical life forms, which prompted him to destroy any droid that would fall into his hands.<ref name="tdr-a2" /> In order to accomplish his evil purposes, Broom established [[Broom's laboratory|his own]] [[Laboratory/Legends|laboratory]], hidden aboard a [[Unidentified space station (Broom)|space station]]. In his lair, Professor Broom would capture droids who ventured on the [[Space station/Legends|station]], experimenting on them before breaking them down to spare parts.<ref name="TO" /> Under the reign of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], droids were not considered citizens, despite their [[Artificial intelligence/Legends|artificial]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentience]], rendering droid [[Torture/Legends|torture]] legal.<ref name="TNEGTD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

Around [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]],<ref name="Polyhedron">In ''[[Troublesome Outing]]'', [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] belong to [[Jann Tosh]], whose ownership of them occurs around [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]] according to {{PolyhedronCite|170|Star Wars Droids: The Adventures of R2-D2 and C-3PO}}.</ref> the professor found a new victim in the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol unit]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], who belonged to a [[Mining/Legends|miner]] named [[Jann Tosh]]. Broom threatened to deactivate C-3PO by removal of his [[memory diskette]]. Tosh, however, discovered the trapdoor to Broom's secret laboratory thanks to his other droid, the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]]. The miner's timely arrival distracted the professor's attention. While aiming a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] [[Blaster pistol/Legends|pistol]] at Tosh, Broom forgot to look over his shoulders. The scientist was knocked down unconscious by the protocol droid, who hit him with a piece of metal.<ref name="TO" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Welcome, foolhardy friends! You're very clever! But&mdash;I call the shots here!|Professor Broom, to Jann Tosh and R2-D2|<ref name="TO" />}}
Professor Broom was a fair-skinned, portly man with [[Color/Legends|black]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and a crescent-shaped mustache. In the early [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of the Empire, he was mostly bald, sporting a horseshoe-shaped ring of white [[Hair/Legends|hair]] around the back of the head.<ref name="TO" /> Because of his discoveries pertaining to the Great Heep and its fellow Abominor, Broom had developed an intense and irrational hatred of droids, which he would vent by committing acts of wanton violence against them.<ref name="tdr-a2" /> A high-sounding yet villainous mind, the Professor gloated over his own cruelty and cunning, bursting out laughing in mid-sentence.<ref name="TO" />

==Equipment==
During his encounter with C-3PO and R2-D2, he wore a scientist's white coat with pockets, green pants and a pair of red shoes without laces. He also kept a holdout blaster pistol for emergency cases.<ref name="TO" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|How can anyone take seriously a villain named after a housekeeping implement? Granted, he is a ''mad'' scientist.|Abel G. Peña|<ref name="Hasslein">{{Blogspot|subdomain=hassleinbooks|url=2013/03/guest-blog-ee-chee-wa-maa-translating.html|name=Hasslein Blog|text=Ee Chee Wa Maa! Translating Spain's Long-Lost Ewoks and Droids Comics}}</ref>}}
Broom was featured in ''[[Troublesome Outing]]'',<ref name="TO" /> a [[Wikipedia:Spain|Spanish]] story that was published in [[1986]] under the ''[[MyComyc]]'' label. In the decades that followed their initial publication, the ''MyComyc'' strips were mostly forgotten, and were only rediscovered in [[2013]]. [[Randy Stradley]], Vice President of Publishing for [[Dark Horse Comics]], was interested in including the ''Mycomyc'' strips in a future [[Star Wars Omnibus]] publication, but [[Lucasfilm]] found no formal proof that those titles were actually licensed, despite the presence of appropriate copyright information. Because of that uncertainty over licensing, ''Troublesome Outing'' and the characters that appeared in it were considered of ambiguous [[canon]]icity for a time.<ref name="Blog">{{SW|url=news/droids-and-ewoks-return-spains-lost-star-wars-comic-strips|text=Droids and Ewoks Return: Spain's Lost ''Star Wars'' Comic Strips|int=Droids and Ewoks Return: Spain's Lost Star Wars Comic Strips|nolive=1}}</ref> However, Broom's inclusion in Part 2 of "[[The Droids Re-Animated]]," an ongoing series of reference articles written by Peña and Handley for the [[StarWars.com]] blogs, brought him into canon. Additional details about the professor's backstory, including his first name, were first revealed in that article.<ref name="tdr-a2" />

The ''Star Wars'' author [[Abel G. Peña]], who translated the story in [[Wikipedia:English language|English]] for the first time in 2013, stated that he enjoyed Professor Broom's portrayal as a cartoonish, over-the-top villain.<ref name="JCF">{{JCFCite|url=posts/50635555|board=Literature|thread=Obscure Droids and Ewoks comics -- translated by Abel Peña|user=[[Abel G. Peña|Halagad_Ventor]]|date=2013-04-11|time=1:15 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150921222207/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/obscure-droids-and-ewoks-comics-translated-by-abel-pe%C3%B1a.50010980/page-2#post-50635555}}</ref> While translating the story, Peña wondered whether the writer of ''Troublesome Outing'' knew the meaning of the word "Broom" in English, judging that it did not sound serious enough for an antagonist. He also noted that he may have called the character "Professor ''Escoba''," translating his surname back into Spanish. However, Peña eventually chose to leave Broom's surname intact because of its "idiosyncratic charm."<ref name="Hasslein" />
